coaching.headline: Another lopsided win: three lanes held favorable matchups, and objective control carried it even through fights we won clean but still couldn't convert.
coaching.team: Carry, mid and offlane held favorable matchups while jungle faced a tougher matchup against Kwang. An early solo death gave them first blood, but the team's objective control erased that deficit. The team kept winning fights without converting next to them, three times taking a fight clean and still losing the tower or ceding Fangtooth in the same window. A full five-on-five at Fangtooth, five kills to one, was the night's cleanest moment, and objective damage finished nearly five times theirs.

focus.title: Weigh the trade before disengaging when a teammate is down: finishing the 2v3 at Fangtooth for a 3-0 kill margin was worth it, but the push that let them take our Outer Tower for nothing back wasn't.
focus.evidence: Drongo died before we fought for our Outer Tower, and we still won that fight, but they took the tower anyway in the same window.
focus.action: The fight after Drongo's solo death at the Outer Tower was still won 2-0, and we converted it into Orb Prime in the same window, even though the tower itself went to them for nothing traded back; judge these pushes by the full trade, not just the loss.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase died three times in the first nine minutes, including getting caught alone for the game's first blood, the kind of early death that hands the enemy free momentum. The carry still only died once before the ten-minute mark, so the peel mostly held, and the twelve wards placed were above Phase's own usual output. Stay with the pack through that opening stretch next time instead of being the one caught in the open.
perPlayer.572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036: Gideon held the favored mid matchup against Zinx: seven kills, two deaths, neither a solo catch. None of Azure Core, Combustion or Wraith Leggings got finished, replaced by Soulbinder and Truesilver Bracelet, and damage landed just under his own usual output despite the kill lead, but that's not enough to blame the build for this result. Mid finished with zero objective damage: put some of that lane dominance into siege damage instead of leaving it to the jungle.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Drongo held the favored matchup against Skylar, yet still finished with five deaths and damage well under his own usual output. Two of those deaths were solo catches late, and the one at the Outer Tower directly preceded losing that tower shortly after. Group up before pushing near a tower alone next time instead of trading it away solo.
perPlayer.3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a: Greystone was the cleanest performance of the night: eight kills, zero deaths, and the most damage mitigated on the roster while still beating his own usual damage by thirty percent. The lane was favored against Grux, and Greystone's team-high mitigation shows that held up. Keep leading the frontline into every fight exactly like that, letting the squishier four follow a body that can actually take the hits.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Khaimera fought Kwang's edge in the jungle matchup and still turned in nearly thirty-nine thousand objective damage, more than double his own hero damage, while keeping deaths well below his own usual total. None of his three deaths were solo catches. That is how a losing jungle matchup gets erased: keep pressuring objectives and structures instead of chasing even fights with the enemy jungler.

12.call: Five kills to one in the full five on five at Fangtooth was the night's best-executed fight. Group the whole team like that whenever the map is fully up for a fight.

19.6.call: Three kills to nothing was a great trade, but Fangtooth still went to them in the same window, with Phase and Drongo already dead going into it. Worth it at that kill margin, but it is their buff running now.

17.7.call: We won that fight three kills to none, with nobody of ours even dead beforehand, and still lost our Outer Tower in the same window.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Phase finished Prophecy, Tainted Scepter and Galaxy Greaves instead of the Marshal and Enra's Blessing core, but the rough opening stretch tracks to getting caught early more than to any specific missing item. No build fix to point at here.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Lotus's random stat roll is a generic pick for an enchanter; Exarch's heal-grants-attack-speed major would pair more directly with Phase's Link-and-heal plan.

572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.build: Truesilver Bracelet's CC-immune shield on ultimate cast covered the same defensive gap Azure Core's low-health shield would have, so the swap away from the meta core isn't an obvious downgrade here.
572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.eternal: Vesh's ability-damage-into-a-burn major suits a burst mage like Gideon well, since his ability kit, including Void Breach, already lands direct damage on enemies.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Drongo finished the Lightning Hawk and Vanquisher core plus Imperator, missing only Tainted Rounds from the recommended path, so the build itself is not what explains the below-norm damage or the two solo deaths.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Weald's low-health execute projectiles reward finishing off targets at range, which suits a kiting marksman like Drongo.

3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.build: Greystone skipped Overlord and Rapture but still built Aegis Of Agawar alongside Tainted Blade, Augmentation and Giant's Ring. This match does not prove the recommended core would have changed anything.
3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.eternal: Nihil's stacking Doom passive rewards staying in extended fights and continuing to deal damage, which lines up with Greystone's zero deaths and team-high mitigation this match.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Khaimera finished Ashbringer, Claw of Hermes and Nuclear Rounds, missing Sky Splitter and Onixian Quiver from the recommended core, yet still produced the match's highest objective damage by a wide margin. No build fix needed off this game.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Exarch's fit data weights it for support, not jungle, so pairing its heal-or-shield major with Khaimera's damage-focused kit is a stretch worth reconsidering next draft.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 physical — predictable; the enemy itemizes one armor item against most of it. A magical pick would split their defenses.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
